articleTitle: Compensation of reflector surface distortions using conjugate field matching
publicationTitle: 1986 Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium
abstract: The feasibility of compensating for reflector surface distortions has been investigated. The performance characteristics (gain, sidelobe level, null location, beamwidth, etc.) of space communication reflector antenna systems degrade as the reflector surface distorts due to thermal effects from a varying solar flux. The technique reported here will maintain the design radiation performance independently of thermal effects on the reflector surface. With the advent of monolithic microwave integrated circuits (MMIC), a greater flexibility in array-fed reflector system design can be achieved. MMIC arrays provide independent control of amplitude and phase for each of many radiating elements of the feed array. The conjugate field matching technique provides a basis for obtaining the required element excitations under surface distortion for maintaining the design radiation performance. It is assumed that the surface characteristics (x, y, z, 1st derivaties, and 2nd derivatives) under distortion are known.

articleTitle: A physically compact quad ridge horn design
publicationTitle: 1986 Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium
abstract: The electrical and mechanical constraints placed on the element design for a very small dual linear polarized broadband phased array has resulted in the development of a physically compact quad-ridge horn antenna. Using its lowest operating frequency, this antenna has an aperture size of<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1/4\lambda \times 1/4\lambda</tex>and an axial length of<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1/3\lambda</tex>. These dimensions represent a reduction in size of approximately 50% over conventional quad ridge horn antenna designs. With this size reduction however, there was no significant degradation in antenna performance. Specifically, a 3 to 1 operational bandwidth with a maximum VSWR of 3.5 to 1 in the operating band was achieved. Other antenna characteristics are dual polarization, 17 dB minimum isolation between ports, extremely broad pattern shape, and a coaxial feed system which originates from the rear of the antenna. This paper presents both the theoretical and empirical techniques employed throughout the development cycle. Also included are measured data for the original physically compact antenna and a second antenna based on a scaled version of this design.

abstract: Long-standing practice has been to view a longitudinal slot in a broad wall of a rectangular waveguide as a shunt element. A symmetrical T or<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">\pi</tex>model of the slot is more accurate. A procedure for developing the parameter values of the T or<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">\pi</tex>is described. The further complication of accounting for external mutual coupling is also discussed.

articleTitle: Phased array beamforming by the Parseval's theorem
publicationTitle: 1986 Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium
abstract: Large phased array provides high angular resolution capability. However the tolerances of array element positions degrade the array beampattern. Beamforming process is essential to minimize the degradation. A new beamforming algorithm depending on the Parseval's Theorem only is discovered. This algorithm is formulated with an optimization process which tries to equalize the total energy at the array input and output. The algorithm places no strick requirement on the input signals and therefore is believed to be scene-free. It appears to be suitable for any large phased array system. The algorithm and computer simulation are presented.

articleTitle: Improvement of the surface accuracy of the nobeyama 45m telescope using radio holographic metrology
publicationTitle: 1986 Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium
abstract: The Nobeyama 45m telescope[1, Fig.1] was designed for operation at millimeter wavelengths. The surface of the telescope consists of 600 panels, the mean accuracy of which is about<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">60 \mu</tex>m rms. At initial setting of panels, laser ranging theodolite was used for surveying the surface. However, the surface accuracy of the main reflector has been limited by the measuring error in the method. To improve the accuracy in surveying the surface, an instrument based on radio holographic technique[2, 3] has been developed. Signals at 19.45GHz from the Japanese communications satellites CS-2a and 2b were used for the measurements. The radio holography using geostationary satellites has following advantages for achieving high accuracy. First, as the elevation angle of the telescope is almost constant, it is easier to reduce the influences of pointing errors and the gravitational deformations during the measurements. Second, signal to noise ratio is much higher than using astronomical radio sources.

publicationTitle: 1986 Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium
abstract: This paper describes procedures for controlling the response of linearly-constrained minimum variance broadband array/beamformer structures. The procedure enables specification of gain and spatial derivative characteristics, over selected bands of frequency, for multiple points and does not require the use of steering delays. An efficient orthogonal representation for impinging broadband sources is developed and used to specify a minimal set of constraint equations for the beamformer. These equations assure that the resulting structure has the desired response at the specified locations.

abstract: The subject of modelling microstrip circuits and antennas on cylindrical substrates is considered. Two efficient methods are presented which overcome the heretofore existing convergence problems for the evaluation of near field quantities. Comparison with corresponding flat geometries will be discussed.

articleTitle: Higher-order mode coupling effects in shunt-series coupling junctions of planar slot arrays
publicationTitle: 1986 Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium
abstract: While the design of linear slot array antennas has been completely automated, the use of an insufficient theoretical description of the coupling junctions in the design of two-dimensional planar slot arrays has delayed the total automation of this design procedure. It has been determined that this problem in the design process is due to the higher-order mode coupling between the closely spaced slots in the coupling junction region. A theoretical model for a shunt-series coupling junction has been created to take into account all of the higher-order mode coupling effects, and then the method of moments was used to calculate the electric field distributions for the coupling slot and the straddling radiating slots. The results of this theoretical approach are validated by comparing the theoretical results to experimental data obtained from a waveguide test fixture.

articleTitle: Interpretation of Kennaugh's physical optics impulse response approach for the slightly bistatic case
publicationTitle: 1986 Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium
abstract: An analytical time-domain expression is derived for the early time impulse response for smooth, convex, perfectly conducting scatterers under the physical optics approximation for the bistatic case restricted to limited bistatic angles. The physical optics bistatic early time impulse responses can still be interpreted as cross-sectional areas of the scatterer similar to what was done by Kennaugh for the monostatic case. It can be shown that the early time impulse response satisfies Kell's monostatic-bistatic equivalence statement. An extension of Bojarski's identity is also obtained for the bistatic case.

articleTitle: Optically controlled phased array antenna concepts using GaAs monolithic integrated circuits
publicationTitle: 1986 Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium
abstract: The desire for rapid beam reconfigurability and steering has led to the exploration of new techniques. Optical techniques have been suggested as potential candidates for implementing these needs. Candidates generally fall into one of two areas: those using fiber optic Beam Forming Networks (BFNs) and those using optically processed BFNs. Both techniques utilize GaAs Monolithic Microwave Integrated Circuits (MMICs) in the BFN, but the role of the MMIC for providing phase and amplitude variations is largely eliminated by some new optical processing techniques. This paper discusses these two types of optical BFN designs and provides conceptual designs of both systems.

articleTitle: Superdirective endfire antenna arrays
publicationTitle: 1986 Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium
abstract: Efficient superdirective array functions can be generated using an optimized polynomial technique[1]. In this paper we further investigate methods for the generation of these functions and study the effects of changing the number of elements and array length on the different array parameters. Legendre polynomials have been used for the first time as optimized polynomial, and results are compared to Chebyshev polynomials where higher directivities were obtained without degradation to the array performance. In this study, an example of an eleven element two wavelength array was used to emphasize the possible improvements from using the new techniques. The difficulties facing the realization of superdirectivity in practice have been analysed for the designed arrays. Optimum separation between the array elements was identified for the endfire case. To illustrate some of the results, we show the radiation pattern obtained from using Legendre polynomial compared to the corresponding uniform array case in Fig.(1). Fig.(2) shows a comparison between the directivity obtained from Legendre polynomial and Chebyshev polynomial for eleven element array for various interelement spacings. The variation of directivity with spacing and side lobe level is shown in Figs.(3-4) for various number of elements.

articleTitle: Theory and design of slot arrays fed by single-ridge rectangular waveguide
publicationTitle: 1986 Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium
abstract: When slots are arranged in arrays, mutual coupling between slots cannot be ignored if a good match and pattern are to be obtained. articleTitle: UHF radio loss in forest modeled by four layered media with two anisotropic slabs
publicationTitle: 1986 Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium
abstract: The radio loss in forest at UHF(2OO-2OOOMHz) is examined for the case that both the transmitter and the receiver are situated in the forest. Considering the scattering of the forest at UHF, the forest is representable as a four layered media with two anisotropic slabs to represent the tree trunk and foliage for the calculation of the direct wave, the reflected wave and the lateral wave. Numerical results reveal that the lateral wave is the dominant wave at UHF and the theoretical results are in good agreement with the available experimental data.

articleTitle: Input impedence of wire antennas attached to bodies of revolution
publicationTitle: 1986 Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium
abstract: Moment Method (MM) in a hybrid formulation that combines Body of Revolution, (BOR), expansions on Fourier harmonics, /1/, and wire approximations, /2/, is used to compute input impedance of wire antennas attached to conductor BOR. A similar technique is used in /3/ to compute radiation patterns of wire attached to BOR. Numerical results of the input impedance of a monopole emerging from the center of a circular disk but arbitrarily oriented (Fig. 1) are compared with measurements, /4/.

articleTitle: Nearfield and site constraints on the design of high performance ILS-localizer antennas
publicationTitle: 1986 Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium
abstract: The currently increasing demand for all weather landing capabilities (CATIII) requires adapted high performance ILS-Localizer antennas. Antenna nearfield effects and given site circumstances set limitations on the use of very large aperture antennas because site reflections are caused actually by the effective nearfield amplitudes. Results of a realized high performance ILS-Loc-2F antenna are presented.

publicationTitle: 1986 Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium
abstract: Printed-circuit radiating elements are useful for large arrays, since they can be easily and inexpensively mass produced. A 1.5:1 bandwidth printed-circuit log-periodic dipole (LPD) radiating element was developed for use in a wide-band limited-scan array. The element is useful in arrays which have scan requirements of thirty degrees or less from broadside.

articleTitle: Adaptive array with binaural processor
publicationTitle: 1986 Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium
abstract: A two element adaptive array for SSB and CW signals is described. The signals from the two elements are linearly translated to audio and presented binaurally to the observer. The observer hears the signals in a perceived space, with signals arriving from different directions localized at different points in the perceived space. The observer may concentrate on a signal localized at one point while ignoring signals localized at other points. Experimental observations are reported for HF signals in noise and interference, VHF signals in white noise and multipath, and UHF CW signals in an anechoic chamber.

articleTitle: Measurement of array element excitations using a planar near-field range
publicationTitle: 1986 Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium
abstract: It is often useful to know the element excitations of an array antenna. This information may be used to adjust the phase shifters of an electronically scanned array, or to verify the design of an antenna with a fixed excitation. It can be difficult, however, to measure the element excitations directly without disturbing the field fo the antenna. This paper describes a procudure to calculate the excitation of each radiator from a near-field scan of the antenna. First, the plane wave spectrum of the antenna is computed from the near-field data. This is divided through by the spectrun of a typical array element. Integration then yields the complex element excitations, which include any mutual coupling effects that may be present. The precise location of each radiator relative to the near-field data is essential for this calculation. Results are given for measurements of a C-band circularly polarized array of potter horns fed by a squareax network.

articleTitle: A thermally opaque, millimeter-wave radome for space
publicationTitle: 1986 Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium
abstract: A thermally opaque radome, suitable for space applications is described. Because of the low-loss character of the materials from which it is constructed, it can be fabricated with little regard for the effects of tolerances. The insertion loss was measured between 18 and 50 GHz and found to be less than 0.25 dB. Theoretical calculations predict that the radome should also remain quite usable at frequencies well outside this band.

articleTitle: A compact high-power feed for a plane-array antenna
publicationTitle: 1986 Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium
abstract: A compact high-power feed for power distribution in the horizontal plane of a C-band planar-array antenna is described. A combination of WR159 branch-guide couplers and of air-dielectric-stripline power dividers provides high power-handling capacity in the limited space available. The series-parallel feed architecture and phase-compensating waveguide sections have a calculated instantaneous signal bandwidth greater than 200 MHz. Four-port couplers and power dividers are used throughout in order to minimize the effect of varying impedances which typically occur in a scanning array antenna.

articleTitle: Satellite communications: Passage to middle age?
publicationTitle: 1986 Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium
abstract: The commercial satellite communications industry is barely more than two decades old and is already experiencing symptoms of passage to middle age: The regulated environment of its early youth protected its market share and promoted investment in space and earth facilities designed to maximize transmission capacity for international point to point telephone traffic among a relatively few expensive earth antennas. The rapid growth and vigor of its young adult phase was encouraged by domestic deregulation and adoption of regional satellite systems by many countries. Because of the bandwidth limitations of terrestrial media, satellites proved cost-effective for high capacity requirements, especially TV distribution. The middle age symptoms of slowing down of growth and awareness of mortality are precipitated by the advent of fiber optics networks and the implications of further deregulation. Now there is much introspection about the competitive position of satellite communications with some arguing that this medium will hardly be used at all for voice traffic and will even suffer in respect to video and data applications unless end to end costs can be reduced. Are satellites then relegated to niche markets such as land mobile, thin route, and point to multipoint? Is this such a bad thing? This talk will describe these "passages" and the role of advanced network architectures and antenna developments in improving this medium's competitive position to secure its graceful transition to old age.

articleTitle: Multiple target detection--Optimum resolution
publicationTitle: 1986 Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium
abstract: A new method of estimating the directions and powers of multiple targets from array data is described and illustrated. Target directions are first determined using the energy distribution of the covariance-matrix eigensystem, and their corresponding powers are then determined using the maximum likelihood method, which are also used to eliminate spurious targets. System performance is evaluated by comparison with the corresponding results obtained by exercising previous estimators under the same conditions: those of Capon, Schmidt, and Johnson and DeGraaf.

articleTitle: Effect of receiver location uncertainty on superresolution techniques
publicationTitle: 1986 Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium
abstract: The effect of receiver location uncertainty on all-pole superresoltion (SR) techniques that use aperiodic arrays will be analyzed in this paper. It will be shown that the effect of noise and element position errors on the target location estimates will be independent. An expression for the contribution of receiver location errors to the mean squared error in estimating the target locations will be derived. It will be shown that element position errors also raise the background level in the image. An expression for the rise in the background level will also be derived.

articleTitle: Metallic losses in a waveguide slot array
publicationTitle: 1986 Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium
abstract: The objective of this paper is to determine the power loss to the finite conductivity of the metal in a waveguide slot array. The method of analysis is based on the introduction of a waveguide slot module. Attention is focused on a single module in which the slot voltage<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">V_{s}</tex>and complex mode amplitudes A<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">10</inf>and D<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">10</inf>(henceforth the 10 subscript is implied for A and D) are assumed to be known values. The losses for the module are computed from the loss-free magnetic field solution. The fields in the interior of the guide are formulated in terms of Green's functions for rectangular waveguide. Explicit expressions for the dominant TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">10</inf>and scattered higher order modes are derived. In the exterior plane of the module, the near field of the slot is formulated in terms of the exact field solution for a magnetic dipole. The exterior losses are computed numerically. Numerical results for a two-by-four array are presented.
